paper.title: Distributed Online Bandit Nonconvex Optimization with One-Point Residual Feedback via Dynamic Regret

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained nonconvex distributed online bandit optimization (DOBO) over time-varying digraph
unmapped: n agents each with private local losses f_{i,k}, global loss is the sum; agents communicate over a time-varying balanced digraph that is uniformly (U-)strongly connected
losses possibly nonconvex; regret measured via first-order stationarity (gradient inner-product) against per-round stationary points
one-point residual feedback: one function evaluation per round, residual with previous round's evaluation
learner's step-size constant M depends on graph constants Gamma, gamma
settings.definition_quote: At round $k$ of the game, each player $i$ selects a decision $x_{i,k}$ from the convex set \(\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d\)... The adversary then assigns an arbitrary, possibly nonconvex, loss function $f_{i,k}$ to the player. In the bandit setting, players only observe specific loss values corresponding to their own decisions

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained convex DOBO over time-varying digraph
unmapped: n agents with private local losses; global loss is the sum; time-varying balanced uniformly strongly connected digraph
step-size constant M depends on graph constants Gamma, gamma
settings.definition_quote: For the constrained convex DOBO problem \eqref{eq1}, we introduce the expected dynamic network regret ... $\mathbb{E}-\mathcal{DR}_{j,T}^\text{cv} = \sum_{k=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}[ f_{k}(x_{j,k}) ] - \sum_{k=1}^{T} \mathbb{E}[f_{k}(x_{k}^*)]$

algorithms.name: OP-DOPGD (distributed online projected gradient descent with one-point residual feedback)

bound.expression: Max(T**Max(a_s, 1 - b_s), T**(2*b_s - a_s)*Theta_T**2, T**(b_s - a_s)*Theta_T, T**a_s*omega_T**2)

symbols.Theta_T: T times sum over agents of sup_{x,tau<=T} |f_{i,tau+1}(x)-f_{i,tau}(x)| (function deviation)

conditions: Assumptions 1-4: balanced, uniformly strongly connected time-varying digraph; Omega compact convex with diameter D; f_{i,k} L0-Lipschitz and L1-smooth
tuning: alpha_k = 1/(2 M k^a), mu_k = 1/k^b, a,b in (0,1), 0 <= delta <= a-b
M = 4 sqrt(3d) n Gamma L0 gamma/(1-gamma)

source.quote: Then, for any $T\ge1$ and $j\in \mathcal{V}$, the resulting dynamic regret satisfies: \mathbb{E}-\mathcal{D}\mathcal{R}_{j,T}^\text{ncv}\le\mathcal{O}\bigg(\max\bigg\{ T^{\max\left\{a,1-b\right\}},T^{2b-a}\Theta_{T}^2,T^{b-a}\Theta_{T} ,T^{a}\omega_T^2\bigg\}\bigg).

results.notes: Regret is a first-order (stationarity) dynamic regret for nonconvex losses, sum_k <grad f_k(x_{j,k}), x_{j,k} - x_k^*>, in expectation. Paper's conditions on a,b are inconsistent (a>=b in theorem, a<=b in proofs).

symbols.delta_s: free exponent parameter delta in [0,1/2) with delta <= a - b

source.label: thm2
source.quote: Moreover, setting \(a = \frac{1}{2}\) yields an improved bound on the dynamic regret: \mathbb{E}-\mathcal{D}\mathcal{R}_{j,T}^\text{ncv}\le \mathcal{O}\left(\max\left\{T^{1/2 + \delta},T^{1/2-2\delta}\Theta_{T}^2,T^{1/2}\omega_T^2 \right\}\right) for any $\delta \in [0, \frac{1}{2})$.

results.notes: Here delta is an exponent parameter, not a failure probability.

source.quote: In the specific case where $a = b $, the dynamic regret simplifies to $ \mathcal{O}\left(\max\left\{T^{1/2},T^{1/2}\Theta_{T}^2,T^{1/2}\omega_T^2 \right\}\right)$.

results.notes: Statement says a=b; proof states a=b=1/2. Table I summarizes as O((1+Theta_T^2+omega_T^2) T^{1/2}).

symbols.M_c: M = 4 sqrt(3d) n Gamma L0 gamma/(1-gamma)

conditions: Assumptions 1-3: balanced uniformly strongly connected digraph; Omega compact convex with diameter D; f_{i,k} convex and L0-Lipschitz

results.notes: Paper's n (agents) mapped to N, D (diameter) to diam_K. Regret defined as sum_k E[f_k(x_{j,k})] - f_k(x_k^*) with x_k^* per-round minimizer.
